items.followUp: What is the purpose of raising the outer edge of a road at a bend?

rubric.why: Identifies how a road is banked.
rubric.description: The outer edge is raised above the inner edge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the outer edge is raised relative to the inner edge.

rubric.why: Completes the definition by describing the tilted road surface.
rubric.description: The road surface is inclined at an angle to the horizontal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the road surface makes an angle with the horizontal.

modelAnswer: At a bend, the outer edge of the road is raised above the inner edge.
The road surface is therefore inclined at an angle to the horizontal; this is called banking of the road.

items.followUp: Define torque and state the SI unit of its moment arm.

rubric.why: Captures the defining property of a rigid body.
rubric.description: A rigid body is one in which the distance between any two particles remains unchanged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body's shape or inter-particle distances remain unchanged.

rubric.why: Identifies the moment arm as the perpendicular distance relevant to a force's turning effect.
rubric.description: The moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation to the line of action of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the moment arm using the perpendicular distance from the axis to the force's line of action.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is a body in which the distance between any two particles remains unchanged when forces act on it.
The moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation to the line of action of a force.

items.followUp: What is the difference between the centre of mass and the centre of gravity?

rubric.why: States the defining property of the centre of mass.
rubric.description: The centre of mass is the point at which the body's mass may be considered concentrated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the centre of mass as the point representing the body's mass.

rubric.why: States the defining property of the centre of gravity.
rubric.description: The centre of gravity is the point through which the body's weight acts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the centre of gravity as the point of action of the body's weight.

modelAnswer: The centre of mass is the point at which the entire mass of a body may be considered concentrated.
The centre of gravity is the point through which the entire weight of a body acts.

items.followUp: How does the value of g change as altitude above Earth's surface increases?

rubric.why: Identifies a reason that the value of g differs from place to place.
rubric.description: The value of g depends on location, including altitude and latitude.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a relevant location-dependent factor, such as altitude or latitude.

rubric.why: Explains how a location-dependent factor changes g.
rubric.description: For example, g decreases with altitude; it also varies with latitude because of Earth's rotation and shape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining a correct change in g with location.

modelAnswer: The value of g varies from place to place because it depends on distance from Earth's centre and on latitude.
At greater altitude, g is smaller; it also varies with latitude because Earth rotates and is not perfectly spherical.

items.followUp: State one use of wind energy besides generating electricity.

rubric.why: States why wind energy is an important energy source.
rubric.description: Wind energy is renewable and does not run out.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying wind energy as renewable or inexhaustible.

rubric.why: Gives a practical use or environmental benefit of wind energy.
rubric.description: Wind energy can generate electricity or be used for tasks such as pumping water; it is also a clean source of energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid use or for stating that wind energy produces no pollution.

modelAnswer: Wind energy is renewable and does not run out.
It is a clean source of energy used to generate electricity and to pump water.

items.followUp: Name one source of biomass and explain how it can be used as a fuel.

rubric.why: Defines biomass by identifying its biological sources.
rubric.description: Biomass is organic material obtained from plants or animal waste.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying biomass as plant material, animal waste, or other organic matter.

rubric.why: Explains a valid route from biomass to electricity.
rubric.description: Biomass can produce biogas, or be burned as fuel; the fuel runs a turbine connected to a generator to produce electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a valid way biomass is used to generate electricity.

modelAnswer: Biomass is organic material obtained from plants and animal waste.
It can be converted into biogas or burned as fuel; the fuel runs a turbine connected to a generator to produce electricity.

items.followUp: State two features of the kinetic molecular model of matter.

rubric.why: States that matter is made of particles.
rubric.description: Matter consists of very small particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that matter is made up of tiny particles or molecules.

rubric.why: States that the particles of matter are in motion.
rubric.description: The particles of matter are in continuous, random motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles are moving; accept another correct model feature such as spaces between particles or forces of attraction.

modelAnswer: Matter consists of very small particles.
These particles are in continuous, random motion.

items.followUp: A body has a mass of 12 kg and a volume of 3 m³. Calculate its density.

rubric.description: Density is mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining density as mass divided by volume.

rubric.why: Provides the density equation and its SI unit.
rubric.description: The equation is ρ = m/V; the SI unit is kg/m³.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing the equation or an equivalent correct expression and identifying kg/m³ as the SI unit.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
